measurements.source_table: Figure 1A heat map and Figure 1B time course (n per group in Supplementary Tables 4-5)
measurements.notes: grade_provisional - grade 3 because the response is frank hindlimb paresis/paralysis, but it is fully reversible. n=3-4 rats/group. Rodent intrathecal acute-inhibition scale (Supplementary Fig. S1A): 0 bright/alert/responsive; 1 tail without tone; 2 drooping hind end or abnormal hindlimb gait; 3 hind limbs cannot support weight; 4 hind limbs and paws immobile; 5 cannot support anterior body weight; 6 forelimbs immobile; 7 death. Acute inhibition peaked ~3 h post-dose and reversed within 16-24 h with no sequelae out to 2 weeks (Fig. 1B). Values at 100/300/1000 ug are reported only as a presence/absence heat map, so readout_value is TBD; the 700 ug value of 4 is stated in the text.

measurements.notes: grade_provisional; n=7 rats. Via ICV the same ASO produced general sedation rather than the posterior paralysis seen after IT dosing, tracking the higher brain tissue concentration after ICV delivery (Fig 1D). Group-mean 3-h acute inhibition score read off the published bar chart (approximate, +/-0.5 on the 0-7 axis); the paper reports per-group P values but not the numeric means. Rodent ICV acute-inhibition scale (Supplementary Fig. S1B): 0 bright/alert/responsive; 1 mild gait impairment; 2 obvious impaired gait/hunched posture; 3 moves away after lifting; 4 does not move forward but upright; 5 lying on side, responds to tail pinch; 6 no response to pinch but breathing; 7 death.

measurements.effect_vs_control: tolerability score significantly increased vs vehicle (two-sided Dunnett) with motor-function and appearance impairment and reduced open-field maximum speed; significant body-weight decrease
measurements.source_table: Figure 1B (tolerability score over time) with dosing detail in the Figure 1 legend
measurements.notes: grade_provisional; 7-week-old female C57BL/6 mice, n=4/group, single ICV injection of 38.4 nmol (200 ug). readout_value is TBD because Figure 1B is a grouped bar chart in which the two day-7 peaks (group means of roughly 9 and 6.5 on the 0-15 tolerability axis) and the smaller day-14 to day-21 bars (roughly 1.5-2.5) could not be assigned to individual ASOs with confidence from the colour key. Late-ONSET CNS toxicity: signs appeared at least 3 days after a single central injection, persisted for 6 days or more and worsened over time. The authors emphasise this is distinct from acute toxicity - no acute neurotoxicity was seen with ASO1, ASO3 or ASO4, and the acute toxicity of ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day. Tolerability scoring system in Supplementary Table S2 covers consciousness, motor function (ataxia, strength) and appearance (posture, breathing, home-cage activity). No recovery/reversal phase was run: animals were killed at a scheduled time point or when they reached a humane endpoint, and signs were progressive up to that point, so reversibility is recorded as irreversible on the evidence available rather than demonstrated permanence.

measurements.effect_vs_control: 2/4 at 1 mg/animal vs 1/4 in the concurrent aCSF control group
measurements.source_table: Table 1 (microscopic observations), brain rows; narrative in sections 3.14.1 and 3.14.3
measurements.notes: grade_provisional; incidence pooled across the 2 males and 2 females examined at each dose level (severity graded minimal/slight/moderate; counted here as present vs not present). Tissue: brain. 13-week GLP toxicity study in cynomolgus monkeys (2 males + 2 females per dose group, so n=4 per dose). aCSF vehicle control or 1, 2 or 4 mg NVP-13 per animal given intrathecally at L4/L5 on days 1, 15, 29, 43, 57, 71 and 85 (0.5 mL CSF removed first, 0.75 mL injected over ~1 min, 0.25 mL aCSF flush). A separate recovery group was necropsied after a recovery phase. NOAEL stated as at least 4 mg/animal. Authors' interpretation: mononuclear infiltration occurred at all dose levels with NO dose relationship, was perivascular and mostly meningeal, and was highest at the lumbar cord/injection site; gliosis and slight demyelination were attributed to the dosing procedure rather than the test item; minimal DRG neuronolysis was seen in a few treated animals but also in a recovery control and is known to occur spontaneously. Recovery-group necropsy showed the same pattern of CNS changes but with generally lower incidence and/or intensity, which the authors interpret as ongoing recovery - hence partially_reversible.

SOURCES SOUGHT AND NOT OBTAINED
- Korte 2020 and Dubost 2025 are not open access, have no PMC record, and the publisher pages were not fetched.
  Only the Europe PMC abstract records were read, and source_table on all 9 of those rows says "abstract".
  Every dose, incidence and denominator in those 9 rows is therefore TBD. Both are high-value NHP sources
  (Korte pools 28 intrathecal studies in 1,016 monkeys; Dubost is a 41-week study with a 26-week recovery phase)
  and should be re-acquired in full text before publication.
- No open-access NHP paper was found that tabulates spinal-cord or DRG degeneration ACROSS MULTIPLE named ASOs.
  Europe PMC searches for Frazier KS returned no hits; the cross-compound NHP material that exists (Korte 2020)
  is paywalled. FDA pharmacology/toxicology review PDFs for nusinersen, tofersen and tominersen were not attempted
  in this lane because they fall to the regulatory lane; they are the obvious next source for NHP histopathology.
- Jafar-Nejad P et al. 2021 (PMC7826274, the RNase-H ASO CNS distribution atlas) was fetched but yielded no toxicity
  endpoints - it is a distribution/activity paper - so no rows were taken from it.
- The Hagedorn Supplementary Table S1 also carries calcium-oscillation scores for all 1,826 ASOs measured in RAT
  PRIMARY CORTICAL NEURONS. Those are in vitro and are a neuronal-activity readout, so they were deliberately left
  out of this in vivo lane; they are available in the saved xlsx if an in vitro pass wants them.
- Papers identified but not mined for want of time, all open access, all in scope for a follow-up pass:
  PMC13040562 (Katsuyama 2026, guanine base modifications mitigate acute CNS toxicity), PMC11229412 (Matsubayashi
  2024, BNA/LNA with phenoxazine), PMC9843489 (Jia 2023, intracellular calcium and acute ASO neurotoxicity),
  PMC11567125 (Miller/Aronin 2024, Ca2+/Mg2+ mitigation of siRNA CNS neurotoxicity), PMC9424863 (Easton 2022, MAPT
  LNA ASO characterisation), PMC12569656 (Yamaguchi 2025, cycloalkane LNA).

HOW READOUT VALUES WERE OBTAINED, AND WHERE THEY ARE APPROXIMATE
- Hagedorn: every score is an exact cell value read out of Supplementary Table S1. Not approximate.
- O'Rourke, Bravo-Hernandez, Moazami: these papers report P values and group sizes in tables but publish the scores
  themselves only as bar/dot plots. Where a bar was unambiguous the group mean was READ OFF THE PUBLISHED FIGURE and
  the row's notes say so explicitly, with an accuracy statement (+/-0.5 on a 0-7 axis, +/-3 on a 0-80 axis). Where
  the bar could not be separated from the vehicle band, or where colour coding could not be resolved, readout_value
  is TBD and the direction/P value is carried in effect_vs_control instead. No value in this file was recalled from
  memory; every one was either read from a table cell, quoted from body text, or digitised from a named figure panel.
- Kuroda: readout_value is TBD on all behavioural rows. Figure 1B is a six-group colour-coded bar chart in which the
  two day-7 peaks (means of roughly 9 and 6.5 on the 0-15 tolerability axis) could not be assigned to ASO2 vs ASO3
  with confidence, so no number was asserted. The mortality rows (n_of_N) ARE exact - they are stated in body text.

GRADING CONVENTIONS APPLIED (all rows carry grade_provisional)
- Hagedorn 0-20 acute tolerability score: 0 -> grade 0; 0<s<4 (author class "mild") -> 1; 4<=s<=18 ("moderate"/
  "marked") -> 2; s>18 ("severe", the scale's maximum, defined as severe signs in all categories including
  convulsions resulting in euthanasia) -> 3.
- O'Rourke 0-7 rodent ICV acute-inhibition scale: 0 -> 0; 0<s<2 -> 1; 2<=s<4 -> 2; s>=4 -> 3.
- O'Rourke 0-7 rodent IT acute-inhibition scale: 0 -> 0; 0<s<3 -> 1; s>=3 -> 3, because a score of 3 on that scale is
  defined as hind limbs unable to support weight, i.e. paresis/paralysis, which the rubric names as grade 3.
  Note the consequence: many grade-3 rows in this file are SEVERE BUT FULLY REVERSIBLE (reversibility=reversible).
  Grade and reversibility are independent axes here and should be read together.
- O'Rourke NHP reflex scale: 0 -> 0; 0<s<2 -> 1; s>=2 -> 2.
- Bravo-Hernandez 0-7 acute activation score: 0 -> 0; 0<s<3 -> 1; 3<=s<5 -> 2; s>=5 -> 3 (the authors define score
  >=5 as severe, i.e. vocalisation and/or seizures).
- Moazami EvADINT 0-75: <=4 -> 0 (the authors state vehicle groups never exceeded 4); <20 -> 1; <50 -> 2; >=50 -> 3
  (75 is the score assigned to a dead animal).
- Histopathology incidence rows: any incidence at or below the concurrent control is graded 0 per the contract.
  That is why the NVP-13 DRG neuronolysis rows are grade 0 (1/4 in the concurrent control) and why the brain
  mononuclear-infiltrate row at 2 mg is grade 0 while the 1 and 4 mg rows are grade 2.

SEQUENCE CAPTURE
- 247 of 254 oligos carry a real sequence; 7 are TBD (NVP-13, the two siRNA duplexes in Bravo-Hernandez, the two
  class-level placeholder entries, the Korte class placeholder and the unnamed Dubost 2'-MOE ASO). No sequence was
  reconstructed.
- Case convention: where the source encodes chemistry by case (Hagedorn) the printed case is preserved verbatim.
  Where the source encodes chemistry by colour or font weight (O'Rourke, Bravo-Hernandez, Kuroda, Moazami) the string
  was re-encoded into the dataset convention (uppercase = high-affinity wing, lowercase = DNA gap) using the
  wing/gap assignment stated in that paper's own text, and the VERBATIM PRINTED STRING is reproduced in the oligo's
  notes field so the transformation is auditable. Two exceptions: O'Rourke ASO1, whose wing chemistry and wing
  length are never stated, is stored exactly as printed with gapmer_design TBD; and the two siRNA duplexes, whose
  guide/passenger split could not be resolved from the text extraction, are TBD rather than guessed.
- ps_count is computed as length-1 only where the source explicitly states a full phosphorothioate backbone; for
  mixed PS/PO designs it is TBD unless the paper states the number of substituted linkages.

UNIT AND VOCABULARY DEVIATIONS, FLAGGED
- Moazami doses ASOs in nmol per mouse. The schema unit enum has no nmol, so the 35 nmol rows are recorded as
  10 mg/kg because the authors themselves state 35 nmol is equivalent to about 10 mg/kg; the 15 nmol rows have

- Moazami's sheep experiment has no matching value in the species enum. Those two rows use species=NA,
  system_model=CNS_invivo_sheep, and say "SPECIES IS SHEEP" in notes.
- exposure_duration, readout_name and readout_unit are free-text per the schema and carry values such as
  "3h_post_single_dose", "score_0_to_7", "tolerability_score", "open_field_max_speed", "mortality".

CONFLICTS AND DOUBTS TO RE-CHECK
- O'Rourke Supplementary Table 10 tabulates the NHP dose column as 30/100/300/700 ug, which contradicts both
  Figure 3B and the main text (4, 8, 12 and 16 mg). The mg values were used and the conflict is flagged on those
  four rows. Someone should confirm against the published figure.
- O'Rourke reports ASO6 at 100 ug ICV in mice with a mean of about 2 in Figure 2A (n=16) but about 4 in Figures 3B
  and 5E (n=4). To avoid duplicate grain, the Figure 5C/5E/5F dose-response series was used as the master mouse ICV
  dataset for ASO2-ASO8 and the Figure 2A/2B panels were NOT filed as separate rows; the Figure 3B mouse panel was
  likewise dropped. Only the rat and NHP panels of Figure 3B were filed.
- Bravo-Hernandez Figure 1A gives ASO A at 3 mg IT in rats a mean near 2 while Figure 1F gives the same ASO and dose
  a mean near 4; the two experiments used different body-weight cohorts, and body weight is shown in that paper to
  be a major covariate. The Figure 1F value was used for the 3 mg row and the Figure 1A sub-3 mg doses were filed
  as TBD/ns rows.
- Rows where formulation, not dose, is the manipulated variable (Bravo-Hernandez NHP magnesium supplementation;
  Moazami Ca2+ pre-saturation and buffer series) collide on the contract's grain, which does not include
  formulation. The six Bravo-Hernandez NHP rows are kept because the divalent-cation-to-ASO ratio is the finding,
  and each says "FORMULATION IS PART OF THE CONDITION" in notes. Moazami Figures 4 and 5 (Ca2+ wash and the
  11-formulation buffer screen) were deliberately NOT filed, to avoid duplicating the Figure 1 rows at the same
  oligo/dose/route.
- Kuroda's reversibility values are "irreversible" on progressive late-onset rows. No recovery phase was run in that
  study; the signs were progressive up to a scheduled or humane-endpoint sacrifice. That is an inference from
  absence of recovery, not a demonstration of permanence, and is stated in each row's notes.
- Dubost's developer field says Novartis. That was inferred from the author affiliations in the PubMed record, not
  read from the article body, and is flagged in the oligo notes.
- One striking finding worth cross-lane attention: Kuroda 2025 shows severe progressive late-onset functional
  neurotoxicity in rats after intrathecal ASO2 (paraplegia, urinary retention, 1/4 mortality) with NO histological
  neuronal death and NO inflammation in lumbar cord, cerebellum or hippocampus (Supplementary Figure S16). A
  dedicated grade-0 histopathology row records that dissociation. No hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly finding was
  encountered in any of the eight animal studies read, so nothing was passed to the hydrocephalus lane.
- All 392 rows are animal in vivo. No in vitro row was filed, including the rat primary-cortical-neuron calcium
  and MEA data present in several of these papers, to stay clear of the in vitro lane and of the brief's
  deprioritised neuronal-electrical-activity category. Consequently no row carries
  challenge_priority=low_acute_electrophysiology.
